blocks.text: An Option is a contract that gives the buyer the RIGHT, but not the OBLIGATION, to buy or sell the underlying currency at a specific price on a specific date.

items: Buyer (Holder): Pays the premium. Has the right to exercise. Maximum loss is the premium paid.
Seller (Writer): Receives the premium. Has the obligation to fulfill the contract if the buyer exercises. Maximum loss is potentially unlimited.
Call Option (CE): The right to BUY. You buy a Call if you expect the currency rate to RISE.
Put Option (PE): The right to SELL. You buy a Put if you expect the currency rate to FALL.
European Style: Can be exercised ONLY on the expiry date (followed in India for currency options).
American Style: Can be exercised ANY time before expiry.

blocks.text: Moneyness describes the relationship between the Spot Price (S) and the Strike Price (X).

items: In-The-Money (ITM): The option has profit. (Call: Spot > Strike | Put: Spot < Strike).
At-The-Money (ATM): Spot Price is equal to Strike Price.
Out-Of-The-Money (OTM): The option has zero intrinsic value. (Call: Spot < Strike | Put: Spot > Strike).

blocks.text: The price of an option (Premium) = Intrinsic Value + Time Value. Several factors ('Greeks') affect this price:
Delta: Measures how much the option price changes when the underlying currency price changes.

items: Theta (Time Decay): Measures how much value the option loses as time passes.
Vega: Measures sensitivity to Volatility. Higher volatility = Higher option premium.
